title: Affine base change gives a morphism of affine etale sites
statement: Let $h:T'\to T$ be an affine morphism of schemes [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. For the affine etale sites of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-etale-site-topos], the functor $u:T_{affine,\Et}\to T'_{affine,\Et}$ sending $V\to T$ to $V\times_TT'\to T'$ is well defined: the fibre product is affine and etale over $T'$. It is continuous, and its induced inverse-image/direct-image adjunction on sheaves of sets is a morphism of sites $g:T'_{affine,\Et}\to T_{affine,\Et}$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0EYL, proof of clause (1), together with Topologies Lemma Tag 04HR

proof.text: Let $V\to T$ be an object of $T_{affine,\Et}$. The base change $V\times_TT'\to T'$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits](1). It is affine as a scheme: the projection $V\times_TT'\to V$ is the base change of the affine map $h$ and is therefore affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](1); its target $V$ is affine, so its source is affine by (2) of that node. On arrows use the ordinary base-change functor of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits](1). Thus it restricts to the claimed functor $u$ on the full subcategories of affine objects. Lean realization: Scheme.affineEtaleBaseChange_isAffine is proved directly by Mathlib AlgebraicGeometry.instIsAffinePullbackSchemeOfIsAffineHom_1, using the affine-object property of V and IsAffineHom h. The definition restricts ordinary base change with ObjectProperty.lift. Steps 2–4 remain an unproved plan in AlgebraicGeometry.affineEtaleSiteBaseChange.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0EYL (lemma-colimit-affine-sites), opening assertion on affine transition morphisms; Topologies Lemma Tag 04HR (lemma-alternative), affine etale subsite

proof.text: A standard covering $\{V_i\to V\}_{i=1}^m$ in $T_{affine,\Et}$ is a finite jointly surjective etale family of affine schemes by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-etale-site-topos]. The base-changed family is jointly surjective and etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change], and each $V_i\times_TT'$ is affine by Step 1; hence it is a standard covering in $T'_{affine,\Et}$. For $A\to V\leftarrow B$ in the affine site, $A\times_VB$ is etale over $T$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits](2). It is affine: $A\to V$ is affine because both schemes are affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism], and its base change $A\times_VB\to B$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](1), with affine target $B$, so (2) applies. Thus this is also the fibre product in the full affine subcategory. The canonical isomorphism $u(A\times_VB)\cong u(A)\times_{u(V)}u(B)$ follows from [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits](3); its target is affine by the same argument.

source.place: Lemma Tag 04HR (lemma-alternative) and Definition Tag 0219 (definition-standard-etale); etale coverings under base change, Lemma Tag 0217 (lemma-etale)

proof.text: Step 2 gives both conditions in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](3) for continuity: standard coverings are carried to standard coverings, and the comparison on their fibre products is an isomorphism. Thus $u$ is continuous. Its precomposition functor $u^s$ sends sheaves of sets on $T'_{affine,\Et}$ to sheaves on $T_{affine,\Et}$, and the sheafified presheaf left Kan extension $u_s$ is left adjoint to $u^s$, by [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-functor-sheaf-pullback-adjunction]. Write $g_*=u^s$ and $g^{-1}=u_s$.

For $S=T,T'$ let $R_S:\operatorname{Sh}(S_{\Et})\to\operatorname{Sh}(S_{affine,\Et})$ be restriction. It is an equivalence by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-etale-site-topos]. Let $h_*^{full}$ be direct image on the full small etale site; its value at $V\to T$ is $F(V\times_TT')$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-continuous](3). For every sheaf $F$ on $T'_{\Et}$ and every affine $V\to T$, Step 1 makes $V\times_TT'$ an affine object, so $(R_T h_*^{full}F)(V)=F(V\times_TT')=(g_*R_{T'}F)(V)$; the restriction maps agree because both use base change of arrows. This gives $R_T h_*^{full}\cong g_*R_{T'}$. Taking left adjoints and using quasi-inverses of $R_T,R_{T'}$ gives $g^{-1}\cong R_{T'}h^{-1}_{full}R_T^{-1}$. The middle functor preserves finite limits and colimits by [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-exact]; each $R$ and its quasi-inverse does too, since an equivalence carries any limiting or colimiting cone to one of the same shape (transport the universal property through the full and faithful functor). Hence $g^{-1}$ is exact. Together with Step 3, this is precisely the morphism-of-sites condition of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](3).
